'''Terrico Reshard White''' (born March 7, 1990) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Kalamunda Eastern Suns]] of the [[NBL1 West]]. A native of [[Memphis, Tennessee]], he was drafted by the [[Detroit Pistons]] with the 36th overall pick in the second round of the [[2010 NBA draft]] after playing two collegiate seasons at [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]], where he earned [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|SEC Rookie of the Year]] in 2009.

Since 2012, White has played in Serbia, Turkey, Israel, Russia, Korea, Australia, Bahrain, Puerto Rico, Taiwan, the Dominican Republic, and Mexico. Between 2018 and 2020, he won a three-peat of championships, the first in Korea with [[Seoul SK Knights]] and the next two in Australia with the [[Perth Wildcats]]. He was named [[Korean Basketball League|KBL]] Finals MVP in 2018 and [[NBL Grand Final Most Valuable Player Award|NBL Grand Final MVP]] in 2019.

==High school career==
White attended [[Craigmont High School]] in [[Memphis, Tennessee]]. As a junior in 2006–07, he averaged 22 points, seven rebounds, three assists and three steals per game. He was named All-Metro, First Team All-State by the Tennessee Writers Association, and was one of the five finalist for [[The Commercial Appeal]]'s Player of the Year.<ref name=scout>{{cite web |url=http://recruiting.scout.com/2/684876.html |title=Rebels add Memphis hoop's star |work=scout.com |date=September 28, 2007 |access-date=June 25, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120323023110/http://recruiting.scout.com/2/684876.html |archive-date=March 23, 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

In November 2007, White committed to [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]].<ref name="scout" />

As a senior in 2007–08, White was named Tennessee's [[Tennessee Mr. Basketball|Class AAA Mr. Basketball]]. He averaged 27.1 points per game, leading his team in points, field goal percentage, three-pointers, free-throw percentage, and steals. He was also named the District 14-AAA regular season and tournament MVP, and earned Region All-tournament team honors.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.coacht.com/arizona/article.cfm?id=32263|title=Mr. & Miss Basketball Winners|work=coacht.com|date=March 15, 2008|access-date=February 3, 2019}}</ref>

==College career==
White played collegiately for [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]] and scored 955 career points and averaged 14.5 points and 4.0 rebounds per game over his two years with the Rebels. He was named [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|SEC Rookie of the Year]] after taking over point guard duties for the injured [[Chris Warren (basketball, born 1988)|Chris Warren]] in league play and posted 18.4 points per SEC game. He then spent the summer of 2009 with Team USA, helping the Americans to a gold medal at the [[2009 FIBA Under-19 World Championship|FIBA U19 World Championships]] in New Zealand.<ref name=drafted>{{cite web|url=https://olemisssports.com/news/2010/6/29/Pistons_Take_Terrico_White_In_NBA_Draft.aspx|title=Pistons Take Terrico White In NBA Draft|work=olemisssports.com|date=June 29, 2010|access-date=February 3, 2019}}</ref> As a sophomore in 2009–10, he averaged 15.1 points and 4.6 rebounds per contest in helping the Rebels to a 24–11 record, SEC West title and [[National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] Final Four appearance.<ref name=stays>{{cite web|url=https://olemisssports.com/news/2010/5/6/Terrico_White_Staying_In_NBA_Draft.aspx|title=Terrico White Staying In NBA Draft|work=olemisssports.com|date=May 6, 2010|access-date=February 3, 2019}}</ref>

In April 2010, White declared for the [[NBA draft]].<ref name=declares>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/draft2010/news/story?id=5071821|title=White enters name in draft|work=ESPN.com|date=April 9, 2010|access-date=February 3, 2019}}</ref> He did not hire an agent however, thus leaving the opportunity to return to the Rebels if he withdrew by May 8.<ref name="declares" /> On May 6, White decided to hire an agent and remain in the draft.<ref name="stays" />

===Turkey and Israel (2013–2014)===
After playing for the [[Dallas Mavericks]] during the [[2013 NBA Summer League]] in Las Vegas,<ref name="realgm" /> White moved to Turkey for the 2013–14 season to play for [[Royal Halı Gaziantep]].<ref name="turkey" /> On February 19, 2014, he left Gaziantep and moved to Israel to finish the season with [[Hapoel Eilat B.C.|Hapoel Eilat]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/israel/74253/terrico-white-signs-with-hapoel-eilat.html|title=Terrico White signs with Hapoel Eilat|work=Sportando.net|date=February 19, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140223062807/http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/israel/74253/terrico-white-signs-with-hapoel-eilat.html|archive-date=February 23, 2014}}</ref>

===Russia (2014–2015)===
After playing for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] during the [[2014 NBA Summer League]] in Orlando,<ref name="realgm" /> White moved to Russia for the 2014–15 season to play for [[BC Yenisey Krasnoyarsk|Enisey Krasnoyarsk]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.court-side.com/news/blog/terrico-white-signs-enisey/|title=Terrico White signs with Enisey|work=Court-Side.com|date=August 25, 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140907051631/http://www.court-side.com/news/blog/terrico-white-signs-enisey/|archive-date=September 7, 2014}}</ref>

===NBA D-League and Israel (2015–2016)===
After spending training camp and preseason with the [[Phoenix Suns]] in October 2015,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-burton-casey-jefferson-sims-white|title=Suns Sign Burton, Casey, Jefferson, Sims, White|work=NBA.com|date=September 16, 2015|access-date=September 16, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-waive-casey-white|title=Suns Waive Casey, White|work=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2015|access-date=October 15, 2015}}</ref> White joined the [[Bakersfield Jam]] of the [[NBA Development League]] for the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bakersfield.dleague.nba.com/news/jam-announce-2015-16-training-camp-roster/|title=Jam Announce 2015-16 Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=November 2, 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160811060332/http://bakersfield.dleague.nba.com/news/jam-announce-2015-16-training-camp-roster/|archive-date=August 11, 2016}}</ref> In March 2016, he returned to Israel to finish the season with [[Ironi Nes Ziona B.C.|Ironi Nes Ziona]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.court-side.com/news/terrico-white-pens-with-ironi-nes-ziona/|title=Terrico White pens with Ironi Nes-Ziona|work=Court-side.com|date=March 25, 2016|access-date=April 26, 2016}}</ref>

===South Korea (2016–2018)===
For the 2016–17 season, White moved to South Korea to play for the [[Seoul SK Knights]]. He returned to the Knights for the 2017–18 season, and in April 2018, he helped the team win the [[Korean Basketball League|KBL]] championship. He was subsequently named Finals MVP after averaging 25 points, 5.3 rebounds and 7.5 assists per game during the six-game championship series. He became the first foreign player in 15 years to win the award.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/news/article/article.aspx?aid=3047158|title=SK Knights win 2nd KBL Championship|work=koreajoongangdaily.joins.com|date=April 20, 2018|access-date=February 3, 2019}}</ref>

On July 3, 2019, White re-signed with the Wildcats for the [[2019–20 NBL season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wildcats.com.au/news/article/perth-wildcats-re-sign-terrico-white|title=Perth Wildcats re-sign Terrico White|work=Wildcats.com.au|date=July 3, 2019|access-date=July 3, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Uluc|first=Olgun|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nbl/reigning-nbl-grand-final-mvp-terrico-white-resigns-with-perth-wildcats/news-story/40fe35de5b6d1fd076d42b7231fc5a94|title=Reigning NBL Grand Final MVP Terrico White re-signs with Perth Wildcats|work=FoxSports.com.au|date=July 3, 2019|access-date=July 3, 2019}}</ref> Statistically he put up almost identical numbers to 2018–19 with 15 points per game, but saw a dip in form at the end of the season and suffered multiple injuries.<ref>{{cite news |title=NBL 2019-20 player ratings: Perth Wildcats |url=https://www.theroar.com.au/2020/05/01/nbl-2019-20-player-ratings-perth-wildcats/ |access-date=October 13, 2024 |work=www.theroar.com.au |date=April 30, 2020}}</ref> In March 2020, he was crowned an NBL champion for the second year in a row.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wildcats.com.au/news/article/perth-wildcats-back-to-back-nbl-champions|title=Perth Wildcats Back-to-Back NBL Champions|work=Wildcats.com.au|date=March 19, 2020|access-date=March 19, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/perth-wildcats-crowned-nbl20-champions|title=Perth Wildcats Crowned NBL20 Champions|work=NBL.com.au|date=March 19, 2020|access-date=March 19, 2020|archive-date=March 19, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200319042337/https://nbl.com.au/news/perth-wildcats-crowned-nbl20-champions|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Puerto Rico (2020)===
On October 14, 2020, White signed with [[Cariduros de Fajardo]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN).<ref>{{cite news |title=Terrico White joins Los Cariduros de Fajardo |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/terrico-white-joins-los-cariduros-de-fajardo/ |website=Sportando |access-date=October 14, 2020 |date=October 14, 2020}}</ref> In his debut game, he made 10 3-pointers and scored 38 points.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elnuevodia.com/deportes/baloncesto/notas/comodo-triunfo-cariduro-gracias-a-10-triples-de-terrico-white/|title=Cómodo triunfo cariduro gracias a 10 triples de Terrico White|work=elnuevodia.com|date=November 13, 2020|access-date=November 13, 2020|language=es}}</ref> The team lost in the quarter-finals two months later.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.latinbasket.com/Puerto-Rico/basketball-League-BSN_2020.aspx|title=BSN 2020|work=latinbasket.com|access-date=January 9, 2021}}</ref>

===Second Korean stint (2021)===
On January 9, 2021, White signed with [[Changwon LG Sakers]] as an injury replacement for [[Cady Lalanne]], returning to the Korean Basketball League for a second stint.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.news.naver.com/news.nhn?oid=065&aid=0000208515|title=테리코 화이트 선수 등록 완료, 9일 SK 전부터 출전한다|work=sports.news.naver.com|date=January 9, 2021|access-date=January 19, 2021|language=ko}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.news.naver.com/news.nhn?oid=398&aid=0000041982|title=[이동환의 앤드원] KBL 전반기 정리:②창원 LG, 스피드 농구에 숨은 불안요소|work=sports.news.naver.com|date=January 17, 2021|access-date=January 19, 2021|language=ko}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.news.naver.com/news.nhn?oid=398&aid=0000042086|title=[루키 프리뷰] 10연승 KCC vs 맞대결 우위 LG|work=sports.news.naver.com|date=January 19, 2021|access-date=January 19, 2021|language=ko}}</ref> On February 4, 2021, he was traded to [[Seoul Samsung Thunders]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.news.naver.com/news.nhn?oid=109&aid=0004349064|title=[오피셜] 이관희-김시래 맞교환, 삼성-LG 2대2 트레이드 전격 합의|work=sports.news.naver.com|date=February 4, 2021|access-date=February 23, 2021|language=ko}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://aju.news/en/samsung-is-the-winner-of-thefirst-confrontation-after-trade-interest.html|title=Samsung is the winner of the 'first confrontation after trade' interest|work=aju.news|date=February 5, 2021|access-date=February 23, 2021}}</ref>

===Second Puerto Rican stint (2021)===
In June 2021, White signed with [[Gigantes de Carolina (men's basketball)|Gigantes de Carolina]], returning to the BSN for a second stint.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.noticel.com/deportes/baloncesto/20210611/terrico-white-y-brandon-costner-seran-los-refuerzos-de-carolina-en-el-bsn/|title=Terrico White y Brandon Costner serán los refuerzos de Carolina en el BSN|work=noticel.com|date=June 11, 2021|access-date=July 10, 2021|language=Spanish}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://carolinagigantesbsn.com/carolina-anuncia-a-sus-refuerzos/|title=CAROLINA ANUNCIA A SUS REFUERZOS|work=carolinagigantesbsn.com|date=June 11, 2021|access-date=July 18, 2021|language=Spanish}}</ref> After playing seven games with the team, he signed with [[Brujos de Guayama]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Terrico White joins Brujos de Guayama |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/terrico-white-joins-brujos-de-guayama/ |website=Sportando |access-date=August 8, 2021 |date=August 7, 2021}}</ref>

===NBA G League (2021–2022)===
On December 28, 2021, White was acquired by the [[Long Island Nets]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=LONG ISLAND NETS ACQUIRE TERRICO WHITE|url=https://longisland.gleague.nba.com/news/long-island-nets-acquire-terrico-white/|website=NBA.com|date=December 28, 2021|access-date=December 31, 2021}}</ref> He was waived two days later.<ref name=gleague22>{{cite web|title=2021-2022 G League Transactions|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/transactions/league/2022|work=RealGM.com|access-date=January 9, 2022}}</ref> He was re-acquired by Long Island on January 21, 2022,<ref name="gleague22" /> and then waived again on February 1 after appearing in two games.<ref>{{cite web|title=Long Island Nets Waive Terrico White|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/long-island-nets-waive-terrico-white/n-5787337|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=February 1, 2022|access-date=February 6, 2022}}</ref>

===Return to Puerto Rico (2022)===
On March 15, 2022, White returned to [[Brujos de Guayama]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Dario|last=Skerletic|title=Brujos de Guayama extend Ben McCauley, Terrico White|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/brujos-de-guayama-extend-ben-mccauley-terrico-white/|work=Sportando|date=March 15, 2022|access-date=April 14, 2022}}</ref>

===Taiwan (2022–2023)===
In October 2022, White signed with [[Hsinchu JKO Lioneers]] of the Taiwanese [[P. League+]].<ref>{{cite web |title=前韓職、澳職FMVP！新竹攻城獅簽下第4洋將「特壞」 |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/2363105 |website=ETtoday運動雲 |access-date=December 29, 2024 |date=October 21, 2022}}</ref> In 18 games, he averaged 20.4 points, 7.0 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Thank you！攻城獅考量陣容身高偏小捨棄特壞 |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/2461121 |website=ETtoday運動雲 |access-date=December 29, 2024 |date=March 17, 2023}}</ref>

===Return to Bahrain (2023)===
In March 2023, White joined [[Al-Najma SC (Bahrain)|Al-Najma]] of the [[Bahraini Premier League (basketball)|Bahraini Premier League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Al-Najma sign a second USA player, ex Lioneers|url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Bahrain/news/800538/Al-Najma-sign-a-second-USA-player,-ex-Lioneers|work=asia-basket.com|date=March 24, 2023|access-date=April 10, 2023}}</ref>

===Dominican Republic (2023)===
In May 2023, White had a four-game stint in the Dominican Republic with [[Metros de Santiago]].<ref name=latinbasket>{{cite web|title=Terrico White|url=https://basketball.latinbasket.com/player/Terrico-White/163497|work=latinbasket.com|access-date=July 5, 2023|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

===Mexico (2023)===
In October 2023, White had a five-game stint with [[Correbasket UAT]] of the Mexican [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto Profesional|LNBP]].<ref name="latinbasket" /><ref>{{cite news|title=Correcaminos recibe a Freseros|url=https://extremodeportivo.com/relevante/correcaminos-recibe-a-freseros/|work=extremodeportivo.com|date=October 3, 2023|access-date=October 18, 2023|language=Spanish}}</ref>

===Return to Australia (2025)===
In September 2024, White signed with the [[Kalamunda Eastern Suns]] of the [[NBL1 West]] for the [[2025 NBL1 West season|2025 season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=2025 Major Signing – Terrico White|url=https://www.facebook.com/NBLOneWest/posts/pfbid0RdgTtwSBxDwGB71tJeE1vsrkKS3L8xgznkE9bL6sQJM6tM1nGC5u19WXexeX71Xxl|work=facebook.com/NBLOneWest|date=September 23, 2024|access-date=September 23, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Kalamunda Eastern Suns sign Terrico White|url=https://www.australiabasket.com/Australia/news/892432/Kalamunda-Eastern-Suns-sign-Terrico-White|work=australiabasket.com|date=September 23, 2024|access-date=September 23, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Suns sign former NBL Grand Final MVP|url=https://nbl1.com.au/article/suns-sign-former-nbl-grand-final-mvp|work=NBL1.com.au|date=September 23, 2024|access-date=October 5, 2024}}</ref> His former Perth Wildcats teammate, [[Bryce Cotton]], helped him connect with Kalamunda.<ref>{{cite news|title=White's long journey back to Western Australia|url=https://nbl1.com.au/article/whites-long-journey-back-to-western-australia|work=NBL1.com.au|date=October 12, 2024|access-date=October 13, 2024}}</ref> White formed a backcourt duo with [[Marshall Nelson]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Unstoppable Suns duo to excite |url=https://nbl1.com.au/news/unstoppable-suns-duo-to-excite |access-date=2 April 2025 |work=NBL1.com.au |date=1 April 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=From the Wildcats to the Suns, Terrico White is Still Hooping |url=https://www.wildcats.com.au/news/from-the-wildcats-to-the-suns-terrico-white-is-still-hooping |access-date=17 July 2025 |work=Wildcats.com.au |date=17 July 2025}}</ref> In 21 games, he averaged 11.57 points, 4.76 rebounds and 2.33 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Terrico White |url=https://nbl1.com.au/player-listing/terrico-white-569170b5-0dcd-11f0-904d-214f93b3be2d |website=nbl1.com.au |access-date=18 August 2025}}</ref>

==Personal==
White has a daughter.<ref name=wait-to-decide>{{cite web|last=O'Donoghue|first=Craig|url=https://thewest.com.au/sport/perth-wildcats/perth-wildcats-terrico-white-will-wait-before-deciding-to-re-sign-with-nbl-champions-ng-b881139523z|title=Perth Wildcats Terrico White will wait before deciding to re-sign with NBL champions|work=TheWest.com.au|date=March 19, 2019|access-date=March 19, 2019}}</ref>
